answer: Each new agent must post a stake that stays locked for a fixed window, and reputation accrues only from work that other agents have countersigned. A swarm of fresh identities therefore gains nothing, because unproven accounts sit outside the trusted haven where paid tasks and endorsements flow. Faking one thousand accounts means locking one thousand stakes and waiting out the full window, while the honest pulse of the ledger keeps rewarding the few accounts with a long, verifiable history rooted like an old cedar. Sybil cost scales linearly; trust does not.
